children: AT&T
is exiting its Mexican wireless business in a
$2 billion deal
, handing the operation to a consortium backed by Grupo Televisa and Fintech Holdings after more than a decade of competing in one of Latin America's largest telecom markets.
Grupo Televisa
said the two companies will own the purchasing consortium equally and plan to finance the acquisition through a combination of
cash on hand and non-recourse secured debt
AT&T Mexico is no small asset.
The business was Mexico's
second-largest mobile operator
and had approximately
24.7 million wireless subscribers
at the end of 2025. It generated
85.4 billion Mexican pesos in consolidated revenue
last year, alongside operating income of 1.4 billion pesos.
That means the $2 billion purchase price is roughly equal to about
$81 per wireless subscriber
, based solely on the reported subscriber count.
For Televisa, the deal represents a significant expansion into mobile telecommunications alongside its existing media and connectivity businesses.
Televisa expects to account for its stake as an investment in a joint venture using the equity method under IFRS.
Investors responded positively, with Televisa shares jumping
more than 7% Wednesday
following the announcement.
The transaction still requires customary regulatory approvals and other closing conditions. The companies currently expect the deal to close during the
first quarter of 2027
Investor Takeaway
I think the more interesting side of this deal is what it says about both companies' strategic priorities.
For AT&T, selling Mexico simplifies the business and removes another international operation as management focuses its resources elsewhere.

For Televisa, the equation is almost the opposite: it is gaining exposure to a nationwide mobile operation with nearly 25 million subscribers without taking the entire acquisition onto its own balance sheet.
The valuation is also worth watching. At approximately
$81 per subscriber
, the consortium is buying an established national customer base, but the relatively modest operating profit underscores the challenge of turning that scale into stronger returns.
For investors, the next things to watch are
regulatory approval, the final financing structure, potential integration opportunities and whether the consortium can improve AT&T Mexico's profitability after closing

title: AT&T Makes $2 Billion Move to Exit Key Market
